newsitem.title: NORWAY: Speculation on new Bosnia force "premature" - Perry.
newsitem.headline: Speculation on new Bosnia force "premature" - Perry.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Tuesday that predictions that a new military peacekeeping force would go to Bosnia were "premature" and that Washington would make no commitment for U.S. participation until all alternatives had been studied.

"I think all such judgements are premature. I really do," Perry told reporters of predictions by German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and others that a new international force would be sent to Bosnia next year to replace the current NATO-led force of 55,000 troops to be withdrawn in December.
Perry spoke to reporters aboard his aircraft as he arrived in Bergen for a two-day meeting of NATO defence ministers to begin discussing whether to extend the peacekeeping mission in Bosnia.
"In the last analysis, they (other countries) will reserve their final judgement until they see what the (military) requests are," Perry added.
"I don't think we (the United States) can have a position until we see what the request is, what the mission is, what the force structure requested is," he added.
